Comments: On 12/21/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Spesak F41 well site following violations issued on 11/16/2023 (IR 3647660, Enforcement 422104). I was accompanied by David Blaker of Diversified. Violations of 78.66(b), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) were issued on 11/16/2023 for the release of production fluid to the ground within the tank battery. The tanks within the battery that previously displayed elevated conductivity readings below the lower valves were tanks 1-3. Readings obtained on 11/16/2023 displayed results of Over range - range up to 20.00 m/S (tank 1), 16.65 m/S (tank 2), and 10.55 m/S (tank 3).The following was observed during inspection on 12/21/2023:The area under each valve appeared as though soils were removed - no buckets of contaminated material were noted on site. The readings obtained during inspection were as follows: 1.14 m/S and 0.28 m/S (tank 1), 18.14 m/S and 12.52 m/S (tank 2), and 1.53 m/S and 1.45 m/S (tank 3) (Photos 1-9). At the valve of tank 2, there appeared to be a sound like fluid/air bubbles escaping. I communicated this to the operator while onsite. Due to the observed elevated conductivity readings under tank 2, the violations of 78.66(b), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4022927 and violations issued for a 1 barrel release of a production/reuse water.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, the gravel in the previous area of the release appeared to have been scraped/excavated. According to the operator's NOV response, remediation (via excavation) of impacted materials was completed on July 30 2025. There appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of the contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.32mS, 0.77mS, 0.48mS. These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67 mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program

Violation ID: 984648
Permit API: 129-27774
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Boro
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/03/2023
Comments: On February 3 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill release reported by the Operator on 2/2/2023 for the Cummins 1 OG Well. Accompanying in today's inspection was Ron Truitt (Penneco Represenative). The findings were as follows:Per Ron Truitt, produced water was released due to the overflowing of the right production tank. The nipple (where the two tanks connect)at the top of the production tank was frozen and did not allow back flow from one tank to another. The back flow not being able to flow from one tank to another caused the right tank to overflow. Per Ron Truitt, it was estimated that approximately 1 barrel of produced water was released. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the affected area in accordance with the spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons.At the time of the inspection, clean up was being conducted. The production tanks were being emptied. Impacted area was being excavated. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. The Department will conduct a follow up inspection to verify that all impacted material has been removed. Based on today's inspection violations are being issued.

properties.content:

Comments: On 08/16/19 at approximately 1000 hours I, along with Environmental Trainee Jessica Morton, conducted a routine complete inspection of the site. The Act 9 sign was in place and the site was well vegetated. The access road was heavily washed out and requires maintenance. The brine tanks were heavily corroded and had poor structural integrity. On each brine tank end cap plugs were not present (see photographs). Multiple holes were observed in both brine tanks. The interior of brine tank 2 was visible through a large hole. Brine tank 2 contained fluid. The Department requests fluid levels from the tanks be provided. The brine tanks were surrounded by an earthen dike. The dike was breached, allowing rain water or any released fluids to escape. The dike did not provide 110% capacity. A container of fluid was observed under the GPU. The Department requests Diversified identify the contents of the container. Diversified failed to notify the Department of tank deficiencies within 3 days of discovery and failed to address and remedy the deficiencies contrary to 78A57(i). The Department requests 1 year (12 months) of brine tank inspections per 78A57(i) be provided to the Department. To achieve compliance the brine tanks must be replaced or remedied in accordance with manufacturer's specifications and applicable engineering design criteria. If the tanks are replaced adherence to chapter 78A regulations regarding secondary containment will be necessary.

Comments: On 10/11/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Blacksville I BIP32 Well in Wayne Township, Greene County in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug a well The NOI was received by The Department on 9/9/2024 and 10/1/2024 due to plugging schedule changes.On site at the time of inspection were contractors associated with well plugging. The contractors indicated that the plugging rig was set up on 10/8/2024, and they expected the plugging operation to take 3 days to complete.While on site I observed the following:-The access road appeared to be in generally good condition. I recommend that the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) installed along the access road receive additional aggregate if contractors expect to be on site for additional time (Photos 1-6).-I observed a silt fence filled with sediment at STA 14+00. I observed sediment that bypassed the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entered a stream identified by E and S plans as UNT to Dunkard Creek. Scouring left of the culvert outlet was evident where sediment bypassed the silt fence. Sediment accumulation was evident throughout the streambed and significant sediment buildup was present within the culvert outlet. I followed sediment within the streambed for approximately 50 feet below the culvert outlet (Photos 7-15).-I observed no sediment accumulation above the timber matting crossing at the culvert inlet, indicating that sediment entered the stream where it bypassed the perimeter silt fence (Photo 16).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 15+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 17).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 18+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 18).-The plugging rig was installed at the time of inspection. All equipment was staged on the plugging pad. I was unable to see if secondary containment was installed at the plugging rig due to equipment being staged close to the rig (Photos 21-22).-The plugging pad perimeter was lined with reinforced silt fence, which appeared to be functioning properly. I observed no signs of accelerated erosion around the plugging pad (Photos 23-24).Due to sediment bypassing the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entering UNT to Dunkard Creek, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, 78.53, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/17/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8211459
Permit API: 047-24792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Brian Ayers, WQS Supervisor with the Department, on December 16, 2024. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on Clermont Pad D. It was reported that approximately a total of 10 barrels of production fluid was released from a pipeline while doing maintenance on a pump. The pump was in secondary containment at the time of the incident. The system which controlled the flow of production fluid had not been turned off before performing maintenance on the pump. As a result, production fluid projected out of the pipeline. It is estimated that approximately 5 barrels of production fluid remained in secondary containment and approximately 5 barrels of production fluid discharged onto the well pad outside of the secondary containment. Upon arrival to the site, it was noted that the pump had been removed and placed on the pad away from where the spill occurred. The system controlling the flow of production fluid had been turned off, resolving the source of where the spill had originated. An excavator was used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. Four dumpsters were on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred and remained on the pad. There was no evidence of any production fluid off the well site.Confirmatory field sampling will occur to confirm full remediation of the site. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/24/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8156531
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 8/24/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator had a rig attempt to drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run would have taken place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. The rig failed to drill down to 550' and it was decided to cement the remaining tubing into the well. Top of cement is now at 288.23' with approx. 102' of tubing encapsulated within the well bore. ARMAC has stated that they have been waiting for a rig capable of drilling this cement plug and tubing out to a depth of 550'. During my visit of the location I did not observe any type of activity or mobilization of equipment at the well-site. At this time the department is requesting an updated timeline as to when work to plug this well will commence again. The violation previously placed upon this well continue.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the EQT - Phoenix Pad S on 6/10/20 @1200 hours in response to CTS report#350244 regarding the reported release of 15 gallons of produced fluid from an evaporation unit. The weather was 79 degrees, partly cloudy, humidity 78%, with scattered showers and thunderstorms in the area. The winds were SSW @9mph. No activity or personnel was observe onsite. The spill notification states "Energy Water Solutions was moving a piece of equipment at the location when the equipment was tilted allowing 15 gallons of produced water to be spilled to the pad surface. SPSI out of Washington, PA was is currently onsite cleaning the spill up. Impacted material will be containerized and disposed of. There was no runoff from the pad. The impacted area is estimated to be 25' x 25'." As of today's inspection, the excavated area was observed. A slightly larger area, ~25' x 50', appears to have been scraped in the cleanup process. Multiple areas that appeared slightly damp below the surface were tested for field conductivity and found to be 0.09mS/cm and 0.15mS/cm. No additional areas of concern were identified. The spill appears to have been adequately remediated. A large disturbed area off the SE corner of the well pad appears to consist of a berm and standing water. The area appears stabilized with mulch and CFS. It is not clear if this area is a PCSM BMP or a pipeline issue. Violations cited against API#117-21115 are cited as immediately corrected. I departed the site @1300 hours.

Inspection was being conducted for the conclusion of a 72 hour Pressure build up test (PBT) that began on 9/16/19. Clayton Shucker and Kyle Jackson were on location from Moody and Associates Inc. The 9x5 space had 100% LEL and 100% methane detected. Moodys grabbed a sample and I grabbed a sample for isotopic analysis. The well was then opened up for Nine Energy Services to run temperature and acoustic gradient logs. Trey Porter is to send a follow up at the conclusion of the temperature and audio logs since they were running well into the evening to complete them. No new violations were cited at time of inspection.

The impacted area appeared to be 40’ in length and approximately 15’ wide with a maximum depth of approximately 12 inches. No discharge was observed off the well pad and the spill did not appear to impact waters of the commonwealth. Violations are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid resulting a release to the ground.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted and INCIDENT inspection of the SWEPI LP - Gee 848 Well Pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 8/23/2019 @1145 hours in response to notification of a spill. The weather was 68 degrees, cloudy, 64% humidity, winds WNW @9mph. SWEPI personnel were present onsite assisting in cleanup activities. CTS report#344583 states "April Heater of Shell notified Carrie Knapp (O&G) that approx. 5 gallons of produced water spilled from a separator inside the pack and some of it leaked onto the ground. They discovered it around 8:45 this morning and are in the process of cleanup." As of today's inspection, what appears to be a line related to the separator, for the 23H well, washed out causing production fluid and sand to spray inside of the well pack. The fluid flowed out the side entry door, and the rear entry door, impacting pad material below the doorways. Due to size of the impacted pad areas, after hand removal of superficial material had taken place, and the visual assessment of fluid and sand inside the well pack; it is recommended SWEPI re-evaluate the initial estimate of 5 gallons of fluid released. Onsite personnel stated a vac box was scheduled for delivery for additional waste to be excavated. Secondary containment was delivered during the inspection. Onsite personnel were preparing to power wash the inside of the well pack, while a vac truck removed the wash water from the rear entry door. Cleanup activities were ongoing when I departed the site. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately corrected against the 23H well: CSL 402b SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a57 I departed the site @1245 hours. On 8/26/2019 Pat Bernethy, SWEPI Env Coordinator reported the revised spill volume is 5-10 gallons and the spill has been fully remediated.

Comments: On March 5, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Oliver East well pad in Forward Township, Allegheny County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3913651. IR 3913651 was conducted in response to the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure which reportedly released 5-10 gallons of produced water to the surface of the well pad. Notice of Termination request was approved by the Department for this site on November 10, 2022.The following was observed:The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 22). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 1). Sediment from the access road appears to threaten a stormwater drain along Williamsport Road (see photo 23). Although no sediment was observed inside this stormwater drain at the time of inspection, a layer of sediment was observed on debris that had accumulated on top of the storm drain grate.The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 3). Well 4H is equipped with a well tag with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be equipped for production (see photos 5 and 6). There are fourteen additional well heads onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 4). An additional storage tank placed within secondary containment was observed onsite (see photo 7). This secondary containment appears to be holding a significant amount of rainwater at the time of inspection. Old GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. New GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 8).A reported absorbent material has been applied to the majority of the area impacted by the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure (see photos 10-12). The conductivity of the soil underneath this reported absorbent material remains significantly higher than the surrounding soil (see photos 13-20). The soil conductivity meter utilized for this inspection was calibrated immediately prior to conducting this inspection. Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and therefore remediation appears to be incomplete. Because it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and greater than 15 days has passed since the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure occurred, violations shall be issued in this inspection report.The Department continues to recommend that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to function as intended in the event of a release. The Department also recommends that the operator take immediate measures to address and prevent potential pollution due to sediment discharge from the access road to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 8168986
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: On December 12 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to IR 3641696.The findings are as follows: The area of a leak around the production tank previously observed appeared to have undergone remediation activities. It appeared impacted soil had been removed and filled in with a fine, light colored material. This fine, light colored material appeared to be holding an excess amount of water resulting in the ground surrounding the production tank to be soft and not properly stabilized. The Department attempted to take conductivity readings of the soil but was unable to dig below the newly placed material as it was so saturated it filled any holes dug back in. Conductivity readings of new material were taken with readings of 0.23mS and 0.35mS. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inquire about the remediation efforts and saturated material around the production tank resulting in improper stabilization. Mr.Greco stated they remediated the site by removing almost 3 tons of impacted material. This material is now being stored off site, awaiting sampling to determine how to dispose of it. He also stated that the fine, light color material is a fine limestone material that was placed in the area of excavation. He insured that the material would stabilize after it dries once, allowing it to compact. Based on today's inspection, violations associated with the spill remain open as the remediation efforts are still being reviewed by the Department. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending a follow up inspection.

Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times. At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator. OGI Adam Hartle assisted in this inspection.

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 924087
Permit API: 129-26518
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/19/2021
Comments: On July 19, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz 1 oil and gas well in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted in response to a reportable release received on 7/19/2021. On 7/19/2021, the Operator reported that a landowner hit a valve while mowing on Friday July 16, 2021 and did not notify the Operator emergency number. The Operator located the voice mail on 7/19/2021 and responded immediately. I spoke with Marc Jacobs regarding the release. Mr. Jacobs indicated that approximately 40 barrels of fluid was lost from the brine tank. Additionally, Mike Walor Woodard & Curran was contracted to evaluate and remediate the impacted area. Mr. Walor indicated that the impacted material would be remediated in accordance with the Act 2 standards. At the time of inspection, The Operator was removing fluid from the fiberglass brine tank with a vac truck. I observed a significant amount of crude oil and brine spilled to the ground and resulted in a flow path approximately 500’ down gradient from the well through the landowners mowed field. The spill appeared to emanate at or near the brine tank valve. I spoke with the landowner, who admitted to hitting the valve with the mower deck on Friday July 16, 2021. The landowner also indicated that it was raining when the valve was struck. The impacted material was not observed in or appeared to have entered waters of the commonwealth. In addition to the spill, the fiberglass brine tank appeared to have been previously leaking and repaired prior to the release. A vertical dark stripe was visible on the side of the fiberglass below what appeared to be two fiberglass patches applied to the brine tank. The Department is seeking clarification on when the patches were applied and why the patched were needed. I recommend that the Operator design, construct, maintain, and reasonably protect the brine tank from unauthorized acts of third parties. The fluid lost also appears to be crude oil. The Department is seeking clarification in regard to the amount of crude oil contained within the brine tank as the brine tank was not equipped with secondary containment. Violations are being issued based on the observations made during this inspection. Additional violations maybe forthcoming pending further investigation.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/07/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/07/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 984687
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/07/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions Pad B after the a notification from the operator that additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) was discovered once rig mats were removed from the dancefloor on the pad. The operator stated in their notification that they believed that this fluid could be associated with the reported produced fluid release from 2/3/23. Two snubbing units are in operation on Pad B. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on the pad. He first showed me the area where rig mats and timber mats had been removed from a portion of the dancefloor. He stated that they couldn't remove any more of the rig mats and timber mats until the snubbing units finished the drill out because the flare stack was sitting on the dancefloor. The fluid present in the area of the removed rig mats had an EC between 3.45 mS/cm toward the southern end and >19.99 mS/cm at the northern end. Mr. Subra said that the clam shell boxes had been placed on this area of the dancefloor which they believed had released elevated EC fluid to this area of the pad. He stated that it is against EQT policy to stage the boxes on the well pad without secondary containment but that a contractor had done so anyway.A crew was excavating this area during this inspection. The roll-off box that they were placing the excavated material in was sitting on the rig mats to the west of the uncovered area but did not have any kind of secondary containment underneath it. The Department recommends adding secondary containment at least underneath the end of the roll-off box that has the door on it. In inspection report number 3492854, the Department noted the presence of a roll-box present on the dancefloor without secondary containment and the Department made the recommendation to place the box onto secondary containment.Next, Mr. Subra and I looked at the area on the east side of Pad B where fluid with elevated EC was found the day prior on 2/6/23. A crew was excavating this area as well during this inspection. The crew was placing the impacted pad material into an unlined roll-off box with a door on one end of the box. There was no secondary containment underneath any portion of the box and the box was visibly leaking fluid from the bottom of the door. I showed this to Mr. Subra and he stated that he thought it was melting ice. I recommended that the box be placed onto secondary containment regardless. He then stated that secondary containment could not be constructed for the box due to logistical constraints. I recommended that at a minimum a duckpond or tray of some sort be placed underneath door of the box. The EC of the fluid present in the area where sample 0718-203 was taken the day before was 15.95 mS/cm.I returned to the northwest area of the well pad and took sample 0718-204 from the fluid present where the rig mats and timber mats from the dancefloor had been removed. The sample was sent to the state laboratory the next day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from the clam shell boxes.

Comments: This inspection is in response to a complaint of a spill on 03/07/2022 located at the Armac lease on Bauer Hill road. The complainant reported a strong smell and saw diapers and oil booms in the Bauer Hill road ditch as well as inside the containment diking. Upon responding to the complaint, and speaking with Vince Bailey the pumper for the lease he reported that the storage tank had over flowed on Saturday March 5th, he cleaned up the oil inside containment he estimated the spill at 2.5 barrels. Monday crude oil had breached the diking by migrating through the pervious material used in the construction of the containment. The crude oil flowed down slope approx 250 feet into a road side ditch on Bauer Hill road, it continued another 275 feet into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Glade Run. There was evidence of crude along the tributary to its confluence of Glad Run. An unknown amount of crude oil was released and made its way into waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 8206010
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren

Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 916954
Permit API: 117-22080
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/12/2021
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of an estimated 20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The operator stated in the notification that a stain was observed on the pad surface on 5/11/21 in a load off area in front of a battery of tanks. This led to the discovery of high conductivity fluid on the pad in this area. The initial electrical conductivity readings of the fluid on the pad were between 15 to 20 mS/cm according to the operator's notification. I met with Matt Tusing of Penn E&R upon arriving on location. The area in front of a frac tank battery where the release occurred was taped off. The area has been excavated but not yet backfilled. No fluid was present in this area or in the adjacent secondary containment. No puddles were observed in other areas on the pad. The water in the stormwater controls adjacent to the pad had electrical conductivity readings of less than 1000 uS/cm. Matt Tusing said that the pad surface had soil electrical conductivity readings of less than 2000 uS/cm after excavating the area of the release. He said that approximately half of a half-round roll-off box was filled with the excavated material. The approximate area of the pad excavated was 45 ft by 45 ft. He also said that the secondary containment for the tanks was pulled back and the EC of the soil there was lower which led them to believe that the produced water did not get under the tanks. No evidence of remaining produced water was observed on the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm.
